# ADR-NNN: {title}

**Status:** proposed | accepted | superseded by ADR-NNN | rejected
**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD

<!-- An ADR records one decision at one moment. The decision is fixed; the
     document is not. Update it as consequences are learned, references
     accumulate, or the status changes — an ADR whose Consequences section still
     reads as it did on day one is usually just stale. What may not change is
     what was decided: reversing or narrowing it means a new ADR that supersedes
     this one.
     The title states the decision, not the topic — "Backends speak JSON over
     stdio", not "Backend protocol". -->

## Context

<!-- The forces at play: the problem, the constraints, what makes this a
     decision rather than an obvious step. Include what was true at the time
     that might not be true later — that is what tells a future reader whether
     the decision still holds. -->

## Decision

<!-- The position, in full sentences, active voice: "We will …". Precise enough
     that a reader can tell whether a given piece of code complies. -->

## Alternatives considered

<!-- What else was on the table and why it lost. An ADR with no rejected
     alternative was not a decision. -->

### Negative

<!-- Be honest here. The negative consequences are the ones a future reader
     needs; the positive ones they can infer. -->
